title: Christian community holds prayer rally in Kolkata against church attacks

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against a series of alleged attacks, vandalism, and violence targeting churches and prayer meetings in West Bengal.
tea.want: They are demanding protection for their community and an investigation into the reported incidents of violence.
tea.changed: Nov 5: Christian leaders held a prayer rally at Rani Rashmoni Avenue in Kolkata following a meeting with an RSS functionary.

summary: On November 5, 2026, members of the Christian community held a prayer rally at Rani Rashmoni Avenue in Kolkata to protest against alleged attacks on churches and prayer meetings across West Bengal. Organised by the Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP), the event drew participants from across the state and beyond. Representatives stated that 48 incidents of violence have occurred since May, with limited police action taken. The BCP delegation recently met with RSS leader Jishnu Basu to seek intervention, citing an unprecedented crisis. While the BCP denied allegations of forced conversions, which they claim are used to justify the attacks, the RSS official called for investigations into both the violence and claims of unlawful conversions. The protesters continue to call for government action to address the ongoing security concerns.
demands: Protection for churches and prayer meetings
Investigation into attacks on Christian communities
Action against those responsible for vandalism
response: RSS functionary Jishnu Basu stated that dialogue with Christian organisations would continue but noted concerns regarding forced conversions, calling for investigations into both the attacks and allegations of unlawful conversions.

updates.text: A delegation from the Bangiya Christiya Pariseba met with RSS leader Jishnu Basu to discuss the rising violence against Christian institutions.
Christian groups held a large prayer rally at Rani Rashmoni Avenue in Kolkata to protest the alleged attacks.
